subject: Sustained token push latency — customer advisory, mitigation steps & closure
messages:
From: Amelia Rogers <amelia.rogers@fastretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Livechat slow responses this morning

Hi Soojin,

We started seeing noticeable slowdowns on our livechat widget around 08:40 PT — customers reported long typing pauses and intermittent stalls. Latency spikes last ~8-20s per response. This is impacting checkout support right now.

I've attached a short trace from our side (stream_trace_20280601.png). Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's streaming endpoints? Any immediate mitigations we should apply from our side?

Thanks,
Amelia
Amelia Rogers
Head of Customer Ops, FastRetail
amelia.rogers@fastretail.com

Attachment: stream_trace_20280601.png (image/png)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Rogers <amelia.rogers@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Livechat slow responses this morning

Hi Amelia — thanks for the trace and the heads-up. We're seeing correlated token-service latencies in the US-west cluster starting ~08:35 PT. Engineering is investigating root cause now; initial suspect is an overloaded edge shard causing slower token delivery to streaming sessions.

Immediate actions I recommend while we triage:
- Temporarily enable non-streaming fallback for low-priority routes (fastretail-support-bot) so end-users get full responses albeit without streaming tokens.
- If you can, set client-side stream timeout to 12s (currently default 6s) to avoid frequent reconnections.
- Avoid large model switching during peak windows (this increases KV cache misses).

I'll update you in 30 minutes or earlier if we have a mitigation.

Soojinn (on behalf of Redwood Ops)
Soojin Lee
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-01T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Livechat slow responses this morning

On Jun 1, 2028, 09:35, Soojin Lee wrote:
> We're seeing correlated token-service latencies in the US-west cluster starting ~08:35 PT. Engineering is investigating root cause now; initial suspect is an overloaded edge shard causing slower token delivery to streaming sessions.

We pushed a targeted routing change at 09:50 PT to move affected premium traffic off the impacted shard to a spare pool. Early telemetry shows median stream token latency improved from ~1.4s to ~0.28s for rerouted sessions; 95th percentile still elevated.

Action items for customer-facing comms:
- Short advisory to customers that we detected a regional streaming latency and have applied temporary routing (include link to status).
- Provide fallback steps (enable non-streaming fallback, adjust client timeout) and offer immediate help to flip those flags on their account.

I'll attach the routing diff and the temporary routing config we applied.

Attachment: redwood_temp_routing_config.json (text/json)

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Rogers <amelia.rogers@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-01T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Update and temporary mitigations applied — FastRetail

Hi Amelia — quick update: we applied a temporary routing change at 09:50 PT that should reduce streaming token latencies for most sessions. We also rolled out a short client-side advisory you can apply immediately:

1) Enable non-streaming fallback on the FastRetail support route (support-bot) — this will deliver whole responses instead of chunked tokens and avoids repeated small token latencies.
2) If you prefer to keep streaming enabled, increase client-side stream timeout to 12s to reduce reconnects.
3) If you want us to do the config flips on your account, reply with approval and we'll apply them (no downtime).

Monitoring is ongoing; attached is the incident action plan and evidence we captured. We'll send a full root-cause follow-up by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Soojin

Attachments: incident_action_plan_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Amelia Rogers <amelia.rogers@fastretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@fastretail.com
Date: 2028-06-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Update and temporary mitigations applied — FastRetail

Thanks Soojin — the routing change helped immediately and our support queue latency dropped substantially after we enabled the non-streaming fallback for low-priority flows. We left streaming on for agent-facing sessions.

A few notes from our side:
- We received one post-incident customer complaint about partial message duplication after a reconnect; the agent workflow handled it but wanted to log.
- If you can confirm whether the root cause was the edge shard overload vs. an upstream cache eviction pattern, that would help our postmortem.

We're good with Redwood applying the two fallback flags to our account (please proceed). Please include any credit or compensation guidance if this crosses the SLA threshold.

Amelia

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Rogers <amelia.rogers@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-02T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Incident closure & follow-up plan

Amelia — confirming we've applied the two flags to your account as requested. Engineering's postmortem (draft) indicates the immediate cause was an uneven shard load combined with a recent cache invalidation rollout that amplified KV cache misses for long-running streams. Root cause write-up and planned remediation:

- Root cause: uneven routing load on the US-west edge shard + cache invalidation process triggered during a peak window.
- Short-term remediation: more conservative cache invalidation rollout windows (no invalidations during peak hours), improved routing isolation for edge shards, updated autoscaler thresholds for streaming token servers.
- Longer-term: adaptive shard rebalancer (Q3), and streaming-aware cache TTLs to reduce mass invalidations.

We'll share the full postmortem doc (internal + customer version) early next week and a proposed SLA credit if the incident meets the threshold. Thank you and sorry for the disruption — we'll follow up with the full artifacts.

Soojinn
Soojin Lee
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
